files.role: Python project manifest. Dependencies: fastapi, uvicorn, psycopg2-binary, pydantic. Dev dependencies: pytest, httpx. Mirror StoryReader/StorageTracker's pyproject.toml structure.

Container image. Build context is repo root. Copies 02_Platform/packages to /platform_packages, sets PYTHONPATH. Copies backend/, schema.sql, tests/. CMD: uvicorn backend.main:app --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000. Identical structure to StoryReader/Dockerfile.

Docker Compose service definition. container_name atlas-habittracker. Port 127.0.0.1:8027:8000 (least exposure — next unused Atlas application port as of this design; see 10_architecture.json deferrals). Environment: ATLAS_PG_* vars, ATLAS_PG_HOST=atlas-postgres. Volumes: ${DATA_ROOT}/habittracker/logs:/app/logs. Joins atlas-net.

Connection pool management plus the one-time starter-habit seed. Identical pool pattern to StorageTracker/EssayCards/StoryReader: _build_url() from ATLAS_PG_* or DATABASE_URL, SimpleConnectionPool(minconn=1, maxconn=5, RealDictCursor), get_db() context manager, init_schema() reads schema.sql relative to module path.

methods.name: init_pool
methods.purpose: Construct the module-level psycopg2 SimpleConnectionPool.

methods.name: init_schema
methods.purpose: Execute schema.sql idempotently against the pool on startup.

methods.name: get_db
methods.purpose: Borrow a pooled connection, roll back on exception, always return it to the pool.

methods.name: seed_starter_habits
methods.purpose: If habittracker.habits is currently empty, insert the five starter rows (10_architecture.json internal_flow step 1). Called once at startup immediately after init_schema(). Idempotent by table-emptiness, not by name.

files.role: The canonical day-model/merge/expected-set/period-boundary module — the single source of truth for every piece of 'real logic' in this app, imported by backend/routers/reviews.py and backend/routers/reports.py. No HTTP concerns in this file.

methods.name: berlin_today
methods.purpose: Return today's calendar date in Europe/Berlin via Python's stdlib zoneinfo (R-CON-AL-06). No DB access.

methods.name: resolve_active_habits_for_date
methods.purpose: 10_architecture.json internal_flow step 6. The single canonical query for 'habits whose active window covers this date'.

methods.name: get_review_view
methods.returns: dict — { id, review_date, status, confirmed_at, habits: [...] }
methods.purpose: 10_architecture.json internal_flow step 7. Builds the full merged-or-frozen response shape for a date. Reused by both GET and PUT /reviews/{date}.

methods.name: compute_expected_habit_ids
methods.purpose: 10_architecture.json internal_flow step 8. The frozen-vs-active-window branching rule PUT /reviews/{date} validates its body against.

methods.name: upsert_review
methods.purpose: 10_architecture.json internal_flow step 9. Performs the daily_reviews + habit_results upsert transaction, then returns get_review_view(cur, target_date).

methods.name: resolve_report_period
methods.purpose: 10_architecture.json internal_flow step 10. Pure date-range arithmetic, no I/O.

methods.name: list_habits
methods.purpose: GET /habits — internal_flow step 2.

methods.name: create_habit
methods.purpose: POST /habits — internal_flow step 3. 201 on success.

methods.name: update_habit

files.role: Daily review endpoints: GET and PUT /reviews/{date}. Thin HTTP wrappers around backend/review_logic.py — no merge/expected-set logic duplicated here.

methods.purpose: GET /reviews/{date} — internal_flow step 7 via review_logic.get_review_view.

methods.name: put_review

methods.name: _parse_date_param
methods.purpose: Parse a YYYY-MM-DD path segment; raises the appropriate ApiError VALIDATION_ERROR on failure. Shared by both endpoints in this file only.

files.role: GET /reports — the grid + per-habit stats + period-level confirmed-vs-elapsed endpoint. Mechanism for attaching the additive period_summary sibling field (10_architecture.json internal_flow step 11): the route is declared `@router.get("/reports", response_model=None)`; before calling review_logic.resolve_report_period, the handler parses the required `anchor_date` query param (str) into `anchor_date_parsed: date` via a file-local `_parse_date_param` helper (VALIDATION_ERROR if unparseable) — a same-named duplicate of reviews.py's private `_parse_date_param`, since that function is explicitly scoped file-local to reviews.py (R-CON-BP-10) and must not be imported cross-file; the original `anchor_date` string is kept unchanged for use in period_summary; the handler builds the Dataset as usual, converts `period_start`/`period_end` (raw `datetime.date` objects from review_logic.resolve_report_period) to `YYYY-MM-DD` strings via `.isoformat()` before building period_summary — required because these values are merged into the response dict AFTER `dataset.model_dump()` runs and so never pass through its JSON serializer; Starlette's `JSONResponse.render()` uses stdlib `json.dumps()` with no custom encoder and raises `TypeError` on a raw `date` otherwise (R-CON-AL-03) — then returns `JSONResponse(content={**dataset.model_dump(by_alias=True, mode="json"), "period_summary": {"anchor_date": anchor_date (the original, unparsed request string — never anchor_date_parsed), ..., "period_start": period_start.isoformat(), "period_end": period_end.isoformat(), ...}})` instead of returning the Dataset object directly. period_summary is never passed as a `Dataset(...)` constructor kwarg. Follows the same response_model=None + model_dump() + JSONResponse bypass pattern as EssayCards' `backend/routers/review_stats.py::_dataset_response()` helper (03_Application/EssayCards/backend/routers/review_stats.py); that helper never merges a sibling key into the dict and never needed date-formatting (its dates are pre-stringified via SQL `to_char()`) — the sibling-field merge and date-conversion are this design's own addition, not reused from that precedent.

methods.name: get_reports
methods.returns: JSONResponse — dataset.model_dump(by_alias=True, mode="json") merged with a period_summary key whose anchor_date is the original, unparsed request string (never the date object parsed for resolve_report_period) and whose period_start/period_end are .isoformat() YYYY-MM-DD strings (never raw date objects); route declares response_model=None so FastAPI does not validate/strip the extra key
methods.purpose: GET /reports — internal_flow step 11, via review_logic.resolve_report_period. Parses the anchor_date query param (str) into anchor_date_parsed: date via the file-local _parse_date_param helper (VALIDATION_ERROR if unparseable) before calling resolve_report_period, keeping the original anchor_date string unchanged for period_summary (R-CON-BP-10). Attaches period_summary using the response_model=None + model_dump() + dict-merge mechanism (see role text above), converting period_start/period_end to YYYY-MM-DD strings via .isoformat() before the merge so JSONResponse's stdlib json.dumps() does not raise TypeError on a raw date object, and keeping anchor_date as the original string rather than anchor_date_parsed (R-CON-AL-03) — not a Dataset constructor kwarg.

methods.name: _cell_state
methods.purpose: Pure function implementing the four-way cell-state rule from 10_architecture.json contracts.invariants. Used only within this file's compute_report loop (get_reports).

methods.name: _parse_date_param
methods.purpose: Parse the anchor_date query param (YYYY-MM-DD) into a date object before calling review_logic.resolve_report_period (10_architecture.json internal_flow step 11); raises the appropriate ApiError VALIDATION_ERROR on failure. A same-named, file-local duplicate of reviews.py's private _parse_date_param — that function is explicitly scoped file-local to reviews.py (10_scaffolding.json backend/routers/reviews.py) and must not be imported cross-file into reports.py (R-CON-BP-10).

files.role: Canonical schema DDL — copy of Sprint01_Core/10_schema.sql promoted to component root. Idempotent (create schema/table if not exists). Executed at startup by backend/database.py::init_schema().

FastAPI app entry point. Installs CORS (allow_origin_regex localhost), exception handlers, request timing. Includes habits/reviews/reports routers at prefix /api/habittracker. On startup: init_pool(), init_schema(), seed_starter_habits(). Identical structure to StoryReader's backend/main.py, allow_methods=[GET, POST, PATCH, PUT].
React entry point registered with Atlas Shell. Routing and all UI views.

Shell registration config. appId 'habittracker', basePath '/habittracker'. mobilePrimaryNav is the primary target (daily one-handed phone use); desktopNav mirrors it, per StoryReader/StorageTracker's shellConfig.ts pattern.

App-local guidance for Claude Code. States the day-model/merge/frozen-display invariants as the authoritative quick-reference, the port (8027), and the schema (habittracker), StoryReader/StorageTracker-style.

route_registration_note: FastAPI path-parameter routes are unambiguous here: /habits/reorder (static) must be registered on the habits router BEFORE any dynamic /habits/{habit_id} route of the same method if the framework's routing is order-sensitive for same-prefix static-vs-dynamic segments (FastAPI resolves by declaration order within a router) — reorder is POST while the dynamic PATCH /habits/{habit_id} is a different method, so no actual collision exists, but the implementer should still declare POST /habits/reorder before any future POST /habits/{habit_id}-shaped route to avoid an easy future mistake.
